1	// Parse backticks

3	import type StateInline from './state_inline.ts'
4	
5	export default function backtick (state: StateInline, silent: boolean): boolean {
6	  let pos = state.pos
7	  const ch = state.src.charCodeAt(pos)
8	
9	  if (ch !== 0x60/* ` */) { return false }
10	
11	  const start = pos
12	  pos++
13	  const max = state.posMax
14	
15	  // scan marker length
16	  while (pos < max && state.src.charCodeAt(pos) === 0x60/* ` */) { pos++ }
17	
18	  const marker = state.src.slice(start, pos)
19	  const openerLength = marker.length
20	
21	  if (state.backticksScanned && (state.backticks[openerLength] || 0) <= start) {
22	    if (!silent) state.pending += marker
23	    state.pos += openerLength
24	    return true
25	  }
26	
27	  let matchEnd = pos
28	  let matchStart
29	
30	  // Nothing found in the cache, scan until the end of the line (or until marker is found)
31	  while ((matchStart = state.src.indexOf('`', matchEnd)) !== -1) {
32	    matchEnd = matchStart + 1
33	
34	    // scan marker length
35	    while (matchEnd < max && state.src.charCodeAt(matchEnd) === 0x60/* ` */) { matchEnd++ }
36	
37	    const closerLength = matchEnd - matchStart
38	
39	    if (closerLength === openerLength) {
40	      // Found matching closer length.
41	      if (!silent) {
42	        const token = state.push('code_inline', 'code', 0)
43	        token.markup = marker
44	        token.content = state.src.slice(pos, matchStart)
45	          .replace(/\n/g, ' ')
46	          .replace(/^ (.+) $/, '$1')
47	      }
48	      state.pos = matchEnd
49	      return true
50	    }
51	
52	    // Some different length found, put it in cache as upper limit of where closer can be found
53	    state.backticks[closerLength] = matchStart
54	  }
55	
56	  // Scanned through the end, didn't find anything
57	  state.backticksScanned = true
58	
59	  if (!silent) state.pending += marker
60	  state.pos += openerLength
61	  return true
62	}

content.text:
Fixed. The bug was in the inline backtick rule's closer-position cache, which could wrongly conclude that a code span had no closer.

**Cause.** `src/rules_inline/backticks.ts` remembers, per run length, the last backtick run it has seen, and once any scan has reached the end of the input it treats "no recorded run after this opener" as "no closer exists". Two assumptions behind that were false:

- A scan that reaches the end only records runs after its own start. When a link label lookahead fails, parsing restarts at an earlier position, and closers between that position and the scan start were never recorded. In `[`a`b``, the scan from the last backtick reached the end, so the retry at the first backtick saw an empty cache and bailed.
- A later, shorter scan that ends at a matching closer overwrote entries with smaller positions, hiding runs a previous longer scan had seen. This broke `` ``` ``a`b`` `c` `` even without any link involved.

**Fix.**
- Added `backticksScannedFrom` to `StateInline`, the smallest position from which a scan has reached the end. The early bail now also requires the opener to be at or after that position.
- Cache entries only ever move forward, never backward.

**Verification.** Added fixtures to `test/fixtures/markdown-it/commonmark_extras.txt` for the three reported inputs and the overwrite case. Results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| test/markdown-it | 297 pass, 0 fail |
| test/cmspec | 652 pass, 0 fail |
| eslint | clean |
| tsc --noEmit on src | clean |

The second half of the `type-check` npm script fails on this machine because the shell does not expand the `test/build/*.[cm]ts` glob on Windows. That is unrelated to this change.
